The Pather plot is foiled, perhaps, for now.

Cedra Keepfaith, a murderer before a score of witnesses, was stripped of her rank before the set of the sun by Archcurate Bywater of the Cathedral of Holy Exodus.

The Knight-Inquisitors will pursue their brand of justice against her, you are assured.

Bornanew's quest is over.

The expression of the Excubitor Orbis does not change. Nonetheless, a coldness seems to have come over him, as if transformed into a statue.

The moment draws out and you think he might not respond, then he speaks. "She is expected."

He remains stone-faced.

The expression of the Excubitor Orbis does not change. Nonetheless, a coldness seems to have come over him, as if transformed into a statue.

The moment draws out and you think he might not respond, then he speaks. "He is expected."

He remains stone-faced.

The expression of the Excubitor Orbis does not change. Nonetheless, a coldness seems to have come over him, as if transformed into a statue.

The moment draws out and you think he might not respond, then he speaks. "Bring him."

He remains stone-faced.

The expression of the Excubitor Orbis does not change. Nonetheless, a coldness seems to have come over him, as if transformed into a statue.

The moment draws out and you think he might not respond, then he speaks. "Bring them both."

He remains stone-faced.
The Excubitor Orbis seems uninclined to make further conversation, so you close the link and order your comms officer to handle the details while a shuttle is prepared.
Your officers make arrangements with the local authorities, requesting permission and receiving a flight path to shuttle down to one of the Knights' facilities on the surface of Hesperus.
Bornanew joins you on the shuttle, his expression closed.
Bornanew joins you on the shuttle. A muted and restrained Cedra Keepfaith is brought, as well.

The simple spacer's coffin holding Bornanew's body is loaded onto the shuttle. One of the spacers briefly puts their hands together, head bowed, after setting it down. A small sign of Luddic devotion.
A muted Cedra Keepfaith is led aboard by your guards. She does not look at the simple spacer coffin which holds Bornanew's body.

Your shuttle approaches an almost floral arrangement of pads set in the midst of a former mine pit.

Heavy doors open from the rockface inviting your landing party into the dimly lit hangar beyond.

A score of armored Knights march forth - like small, segmented dolls compared with the scale of the door, but as you approach you note their height. They must be the tallest farm-fed children of Gilead and Tartessus, all aclad in polished white armor, half-capes slack in the near-vacuum.

They turn precisely aside, weapons held vertical.

You enter, the guards reverse their process, and the hangar is pressurized. 

A far door cracks open, casting a long wedge of light. Spots snap on, converted shuttles and fightercraft loom in all corners.

The Excubitor Orbis enters. 

Gideon Oak is a brick of a man, squat but powerful. Perhaps the product of a forgotten high-G world. He is accompanied by a weedy clerk.

"Captain $playerName," the Excubitor Orbis nods, his voice gravelly.

His dark eyes take in the spacer's coffin carried by your entourage. You turn to give them a nod, and they set the coffin on the floor of the hangar.  

"Novice Bornanew," he says.

"Captain $playerName," the Excubitor Orbis nods, his voice gravelly.

His dark eyes take in the spacer's coffin carried by your entourage. You turn to give them a nod, and they set the coffin on the floor of the hangar.  

"Novice Bornanew," he says.

He seems to be ignoring Keepfaith entirely. For now.

"Captain $playerName," the Excubitor Orbis nods, his voice gravelly.

His dark eyes take in Knight-Novice Bornanew beside you. He wears a light vac suit and bears his small satchel of possessions in one hand and the sample case with the false relic glove in the other. He insisted that he needed no help with it.

"Novice Bornanew," Oak says.

Gideon Oak shifts his stony gaze to you.

"Tell me how," he says.

Keepfaith inhales as if she might speak, some righteous outburst, but falters. Her eyes fall back toward the ground.

The Excubitor Orbis takes in your comment, his face impassive as the stone this hangar was blasted from. His clerk's eyes are downcast.

Is that a twitch of impatience on the impassive face of the Excubitor Orbis? But truly, the read is in his clerk; she almost cringes at the insufficiency of your answer.

Oak lets out a slow breath.

"So be it," he says, looking away as if you're no longer worth his time.

The Excubitor Orbis takes in your comment, his face impassive as the stone this hangar was blasted from.

His clerk's eyes are downcast.

Is that a twitch of impatience on the impassive face of the Excubitor Orbis? But truly, the read is in his clerk; she almost cringes at the insufficiency of your answer.

Oak lets out a slow breath, and looks away from you as if your words are worth nothing to him. He makes a subtle movement with his hand.

Is that a twitch of impatience on the impassive face of the Excubitor Orbis? But truly, the read is in his clerk; she almost cringes at the insufficiency of your answer.

Oak lets out a slow breath. "So be it," he says, looking away, as if you're not worth his time.

A quartet of armored Knights take this as their cue to approach Bornanew's coffin. Together, without needing a signal, they lift as one and bear him toward the door at the far end of the hangar. Their silhouettes make long shadows in the wedge of warm light.

The stony gaze of Gideon Oak then turns slowly toward the prisoner in a simple e-suit and bound by hand-restraints - a bit of symbolism more than security measure  - flanked by your guards.

"Keepfaith," he says.

She inhales as if she might speak, some righteous outburst, but falters. Her eyes fall toward the ground.

The stony gaze of Gideon Oak turns slowly toward the prisoner in a simple temp suit with hand-restraints - a bit of symbolism more than security measure  - flanked by your guards.

"Keepfaith," he says.

She inhales as if she might speak, some righteous outburst, but falters. Her eyes fall toward the ground.

Oak lets out a slow breath.

He makes a subtle movement with his hand, and a pair of the huge, armored guards step to Keepfaith.

Faceless in their armor, they take her away.

You are left with Oak, his clerk, and Bornanew.

"The glove," says the Excubitor Orbis.

You are left with Oak, his clerk, and the coffin of Bornanew.

"And the glove," says the Excubitor Orbis.

The Excubitor Orbis had never stopped watching you. "Your theory. Tartessus," he prompts $global.jethroName.

Bornanew takes a step forward. "Excubitor Orbis. We tracked the source of the false relic to a nanoforge operated by heretics of the so-called Luddic Path. A station on the far fringe, in the $bffi_patherStationSystem."

He glances at you. "Captain $playerName procured datastores from the station, and the forge, before destroying both. I found communications involving the Subcurate Cedra Keepfaith in the Cathedral of Holy Exodus. I confronted her directly. She interfered with Knight-Captain Larix's weapon and I... was shot."

Oak's eyes narrow, which is enough to prompt silence. Oak's clerk looks between him and Bornanew curiously, but she also holds her tongue.

"Keepfaith fled and has not been found," Bornanew continues. "The Reverend Archcurate Bywater, of the Cathedral of Holy Exodus, saw fit to strip her of the station of Subcurate in absentia."

The Excubitor Orbis had never stopped watching you. "Your theory. Tartessus," he prompts $global.jethroName.

Bornanew steps forward. "I tracked the source of the false relic to a nanoforge operated by Pather heretics. A godless hive of a station on the far fringe, in the $bffi_patherStationSystem."

He doesn't look at you, but speaks directly. "Captain $playerName seized datastores from the station, and the forge, before destroying both. I discovered communications involving a traitor, the Subcurate Cedra Keepfaith of the Cathedral of Holy Exodus. I confronted her directly with her crime. She interfered with Knight-Captain Larix's weapon and shot me."

Oak's eyes narrow. Oak's clerk looks between him and Bornanew curiously, but she also holds her tongue.

"The traitor fled and the Knights posted to Tartessus have not found her," Bornanew continues, criticism obvious in his tone. "The Reverend Archcurate Bywater, of the Cathedral of Holy Exodus, saw fit to strip Keepfaith of the station of Subcurate in absentia. Nonetheless, she has thus far escaped punishment. If you simply order the Inquisitors to-"

Gideon Oak raises a hand, almost a parody of the gesture frozen in the glove that started this all. Bornanew silences himself with obvious reluctance.

Oak's clerk finally speaks up, glancing down at her notebook then at the Excubitor Orbis, then you.

"The subcur... the accused, Cedra Keepfaith, is in the custody of our order. She is... with the Inquisitors now."

She folds her notebook away. The Excubitor Orbis does not change his expression.

Oak's clerk finally speaks up, glancing down at her notebook then at the Excubitor Orbis, then you.

"The subcur... the accused, Cedra Keepfaith, has been added to watchlists throughout the ecumene. The Heretic-finders of the Inquisition have taken responsibility for the situation."

She folds her notebook away. The Excubitor Orbis does not change his expression.

The Excubitor Orbis had never stopped watching you. "Your theory. Tartessus," he prompts $global.jethroName.

Bornanew steps forward. "We tracked the source of the false relic to a nanoforge operated by heretics of the so-called Luddic Path. A station on the far fringe, in the $bffi_patherStationSystem."

He glances at you. "The station, and the nanoforge, were annihilated. We did not find evidence of a mole in the Cathedral of Holy Exodus. Humbly, sir, if you would allow-"

Oak's eyes narrow, which is enough to prompt silence. Oak's clerk looks between him and Bornanew curiously, but she also holds her tongue.

He does not look at you, but continues. "We destroyed the station and the nanoforge. We have not found additional evidence of the mole in the Cathedral of Holy Exodus. The Inquisition should simply declare-"

Oak's eyes narrow, which is enough to prompt silence, though $global.jethroName bridles to contain himself. Oak's clerk looks between the Excubitor Orbis and Bornanew curiously, and she too holds her tongue.

Bornanew bows, then places the sample container he was carrying on the hangar floor.

Without rush or flourish, he unlatches the cover and withdraws it to reveal the false relic, the upthrust work-glove which was never touched by Ludd.
